entities.summary:
Du Qiong, courtesy name Boyu, was an official, astronomer and diviner of the state of Shu Han in the Three Kingdoms period of China. He was appointed as a high-ranking official and served under the rule of Liu Shan, the last emperor of the Shu Han state. Du Qiong was responsible for overseeing the state's astronomical observations and was known for his expertise in predicting celestial events.

Du Qiong's contributions to the field of astronomy were significant, and he played a crucial role in the development of the astronomical observations of the Shu Han state. His work built upon the knowledge of the ancient Chinese astronomers, who had made significant contributions to the field over the centuries. Du Qiong's legacy continued to influence astronomical observations in China for centuries after his death.

Du Qiong's significance in the context of the Three Kingdoms period lies in his role as a key figure in the state's administration and his contributions to the field of astronomy. His work highlights the importance of scientific inquiry and observation in understanding the natural world.

Du Qiong's impact on history can be seen in the continued influence of his astronomical observations on the development of Chinese astronomy. His work serves as a testament to the importance of scientific inquiry and the need for continued observation and study of the natural world.
